id: title:EDsCODE:preserve logical fields during trino resolution

observations.behavior: Adds a `physical_names=False` argument to the structural lowering pass before type resolution.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows HogQL query planning and warehouse printing to preserve logical field names while omitting redundant physical column metadata. This could prevent unnecessary schema bloat or name collisions when generating queries for warehouses that distinguish between source and target identifiers.

observations.behavior: Changes how column names are selected during any join transformations: either use stored database field names (physical) or keep original AST names.
observations.posthog_connection: Supports warehouse-specific behavior where joins must retain user-facing logical names rather than backend-internal physical names, potentially improving compatibility with warehouse dialects like DuckDB/Trino that require explicit qualification or disallow implicit aliasing of shared columns.

observations.behavior: Makes the replacement of bare fields with resolved database field names conditional on whether physical names should be exposed.
observations.posthog_connection: Preserves semantic identity in generated SQL by not replacing logical aliases unless explicitly requested; this supports warehouse callers who rely on curated definitions without exposing internal implementation details.

observations.limitations: All changes are confined to HogQL printer and Trino transformation helpers; no end-to-end integration tests, production configuration updates, or migration paths are shown. The documentation change is isolated and does not demonstrate runtime enforcement.

review.limitations: All changes are confined to HogQL printer and Trino transformation helpers; no end-to-end integration tests, production configuration updates, or migration paths are shown. The documentation change is isolated and does not demonstrate runtime enforcement.
review.reason: Adds a bounded capability—supporting warehouse callers who need preserved logical names while omitting redundant physical metadata—with supporting parameterized unit tests and localized implementation across three hunks. No broader systemic risk reduction or adoption evidence is demonstrated.
review.posthog_relevance: Relevant for PostHog’s warehouse ingestion and query planning workflows, particularly when generating compatible SQL against warehouses that distinguish between source and target identifiers.
review.uncertainty: Changes could have downstream effects on compatibility but lack complete execution context; tier remains conservative.
